Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the HealthNet Hospitals, Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. [Standard operator instructions for Q&A instructions will follow the prepared remarks.]

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HealthNet Hospitals, Inc.'s financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Mark Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Sarah Kline, Chief Medical Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Strategy Officer; and David Kim, Chief Information Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter of 2024. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency across our portfolio of over 100 acute care hospitals and numerous outpatient facilities nationwide.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on seven key aspects: operating margin year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, an overview of key financial performance highlights, operating margin guidance for the next quarter and full year, trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, net patient revenue year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, revenue per admission trends and drivers, and the percentage of revenue from Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and self-pay.

These metrics highlight our disciplined approach in a challenging environment marked by labor inflation, supply chain issues, and regulatory pressures. Now, I'll turn the call over to Mark to provide a more detailed review of our financial results, where he'll expand on these areas.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Vasquez mentioned, we had a strong quarter across the board. Let me dive deeper into these critical aspects, starting with our operating margin performance, which continues to reflect the strength of our operational discipline amid macroeconomic and regulatory headwinds in the healthcare services sector. Operating margin—defined as adjusted operating income divided by net patient service revenues plus other operating revenues—is a key metric for us, capturing our ability to convert top-line growth into bottom-line profitability while navigating industry challenges like labor inflation, supply chain disruptions, and shifting payer mixes.

For Q3 2024, we delivered an operating margin of 12.5%, marking a robust 230 basis point expansion year-over-year from 10.2% in Q3 2023, and a solid 70 basis point improvement quarter-over-quarter from 11.8% in Q2 2024. This performance exceeded our internal guidance of 11.5% to 12.0% and positions us at the high end of the ZS Associates Hospital Operating Margin Index for large acute-care systems, which averaged 9.8% for the quarter across peers like HCA Healthcare and Tenet Healthcare.

Breaking down the year-over-year expansion, revenue growth was the primary tailwind, up 8.2% to $2.85 billion, fueled by a 5.1% increase in equivalent patient days—driven by higher acuity inpatient volumes, particularly in cardiology and orthopedics, as elective procedures fully normalized post-COVID—and a 12% ramp in outpatient services, including our ambulatory surgery centers, which now represent 22% of total revenues, up from 18% a year ago. Case mix index improved 2.3% year-over-year to 1.82, reflecting our strategic focus on high-margin service lines like robotic-assisted joint replacements using the Mako system from Stryker, which boosted ortho margins by 150 basis points.

On the cost side, we achieved disciplined expense management. Total operating expenses grew only 5.9% year-over-year, well below revenue growth, thanks to several initiatives. Labor costs, which comprise 52% of our cost base, rose 6.8% but decelerated from 9.2% in the prior quarter, as our nurse retention program—offering $15,000 sign-on bonuses and 15% premium pay for travel nurses—stabilized staffing at 95% of budgeted levels, up from 88% last year. We also improved productivity metrics, with hours per equivalent patient day advancing 4.2% year-over-year to 18.2 hours, aided by our AI-powered workforce scheduling platform from LeanTaaS, which optimized shift utilization across our 45-hospital footprint in key regions.

Supply expenses, at 18% of revenues, increased 7.1% year-over-year due to persistent pharmaceutical inflation—such as GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic driving up endocrine service costs—but we mitigated this through our group purchasing organization partnership with Vizient, securing 3-5% better pricing on high-volume items like implants and contrast media. Revenue cycle management enhancements via our Epic EHR optimization project yielded a 120 basis point year-over-year improvement in cash collection rates to 98.1%, with days in accounts receivable steady at 42 days.

Regionally, performance varied but trended positively. In our high-growth Sunbelt markets—Florida, Texas, and Arizona, accounting for 55% of our bed capacity—margins expanded 310 basis points year-over-year to 14.2%, benefiting from favorable demographics, Medicare Advantage penetration now at 32% of lives up from 28%, and lower Medicaid mix at 18%. Urban clusters like our Miami-Dade and Dallas-Fort Worth facilities saw outsized gains from commercial payer reimbursements averaging 145% of Medicare rates versus 135% nationally. Our Northeast and Midwest regions, 35% of capacity, improved a more modest 150 basis points to 10.8%, pressured by regulatory caps on commercial rates in New York and Illinois and higher unionized labor costs—though our telehealth expansion to 25% of visits helped offset volume softness from seasonal flu variances.

Quarter-over-quarter, the 70 basis point lift from Q2 reflects seasonal tailwinds and operational momentum. Inpatient volumes rebounded 3.2% from winter peaks, while our value-based care contracts with UnitedHealthcare and Blue Cross Blue Shield—covering 15% of our lives—delivered shared savings of $18 million, up 25% quarter-over-quarter, as we hit quality metrics in readmissions down to 14.2% from 15.1% and sepsis bundles. Non-labor costs deleveraged further, with supply chain analytics from our GHX integration reducing variance by 2.1% quarter-over-quarter.

These margins underscore our 'High Reliability, High Margin' framework. We've accelerated investments in digital health: $45 million in Q3 for AI-driven clinical decision support from Nuance, now part of Microsoft, to enhance coding accuracy and reduce denials by 18%; and a $200 million tuck-in acquisition of three ASCs in Texas, targeting 18% margins in that segment. Looking ahead briefly, we expect continued pressure from the CMS FY2025 IPPS update—flat 2.9% increase but with site-neutral payment cuts impacting outpatient HOPDs—but our payer negotiations aim for 4-5% commercial rate hikes.

In summary on margins, our 12.5% result reflects resilient execution in a sector where Kaufman Hall reports median margins lagging at 8.5%. We're proud to outperform peers like Community Health Systems at 7.2% this quarter and remain committed to 13%+ long-term through scale, technology, and service-line optimization.

Building on that, let's turn to an overview of our key financial performance highlights, which reflect a resilient quarter amid ongoing industry headwinds like persistent labor inflation, supply chain pressures, and moderating reimbursement rates from CMS under the IPPS final rule. HealthNet Hospitals operates a diversified portfolio of 120 acute care hospitals and over 300 outpatient facilities across 22 states, with a strong footprint in high-growth Sunbelt markets like Texas, Florida, and Arizona, complemented by mature operations in the Midwest and Southeast.

Starting with the top line, we delivered consolidated net revenues of $4.8 billion for Q3, up 6.2% year-over-year, or 7.1% on a same-facility basis excluding divestitures. This marks our 10th consecutive quarter of revenue growth, driven by modest volume expansion, favorable payer mix shifts, and disciplined pricing strategies. Inpatient revenues grew 4.8% to $2.9 billion, reflecting 2.1% growth in admissions to 142,000—our strongest quarterly print since Q1 2023—bolstered by higher acuity cases, with case-mix index up 1.4% to 1.72. Outpatient revenues, now 42% of total revenues, surged 9.5% to $1.8 billion, fueled by a 12% increase in surgical cases to 185,000, including strong uptake in high-margin procedures like orthopedics and cardiology at our ASCs. Emergency department visits rose 3.7% to 1.1 million, though we saw some normalization in non-emergent volumes post-COVID backlog.

Pricing dynamics remain supportive, with net patient revenue per admission climbing 2.6% to $20,450, benefiting from commercial rate improvements averaging 4.2% in renewals and a stable payer mix: commercial insurance steady at 48%, Medicare at 38% despite a 2.9% reimbursement cut under the FY24 IPPS, and Medicaid at 14%. Length of stay held flat at 4.6 days, reflecting our focus on operational efficiency through proprietary CarePathway protocols, which reduced LOS by 0.2 days in high-volume DRGs such as sepsis and heart failure.

Turning to profitability, adjusted EBITDA reached $785 million, up 8.4% year-over-year, with margins expanding 50 basis points to 16.4%—outpacing our hospital peer group as reported by Kaufman Hall, where medians sit at 14.8%. This stems from 320 basis point outperformance on labor costs as a percentage of revenue, now at 52.1% after aggressive staffing optimization via 25% quarter-over-quarter travel nurse reductions and our UnityFlex float pool model covering 18% of nursing hours internally. Supply costs rose 6.8% due to pharmaceutical inflation and orthopedic implant pricing, but we mitigated via our GPO partnership with Vizient, achieving $45 million in year-to-date savings via contract rebids. Non-labor expenses, including contract labor and professional fees, were controlled at 18.3% of revenue.

On the bottom line, net income attributable to HealthNet Hospitals came in at $325 million, or $1.42 diluted EPS, up 11% and 12% respectively from last year. Adjusted EPS, excluding non-recurring items like our $28 million gain on the sale of a low-performing Midwest facility, was $1.68, beating consensus by $0.09. Cash flow from operations was robust at $920 million for the quarter, supporting $450 million in capital expenditures—primarily for Epic MyChart upgrades across 65 hospitals, da Vinci Xi robotic systems in 12 new ORs, and de novo ASC developments in Phoenix and Dallas-Fort Worth.

Our balance sheet remains fortress-like, with net debt to adjusted EBITDA at 3.1x, down from 3.4x at year-end 2023, and $1.2 billion in liquidity. We repurchased $150 million in shares under our $1 billion authorization and raised our quarterly dividend by 5% to $0.22 per share.

Regionally, Sunbelt markets drove 65% of growth, with Texas same-facility revenues up 11% on 5% admission growth and Florida ASC volumes surging 18% amid Medicare Advantage penetration. Midwest operations faced softer demand with admissions flat, but EBITDA margins held at 15.2% through cost discipline. Nationally, we're navigating nurse staffing ratios in California and wage pressures in urban centers, offset by rural hospital stabilization grants totaling $12 million received this quarter.

Strategically, these results underscore our "Growth + Efficiency" framework. We've advanced value-based care with 45% of Medicare lives under ACO REACH 2.0, generating $68 million in shared savings, and launched AI-powered revenue cycle management via our partnership with Olive AI—early pilots show a 22% reduction in denial rates. M&A remains opportunistic; we closed a $275 million tuck-in acquisition of three Tenet-affiliated hospitals in Georgia, accretive immediately at 14x EBITDA multiple. Looking ahead, we're raising FY24 guidance: revenues to $19.0-$19.3 billion, adjusted EBITDA to $3.15-$3.25 billion, and adjusted EPS to $6.75-$6.95, implying 7-9% growth.

Next, on operating margin guidance for Q4 and FY 2025. For the fourth quarter of 2024, we are guiding to an operating margin in the range of 8.2% to 8.8%, representing a sequential improvement of approximately 50 to 110 basis points from our Q3 reported margin of 7.3%. This outlook assumes continued same-facility revenue growth of 4.5% to 5.5%, driven by inpatient and outpatient volume increases of 2.0% to 3.0% and modest pricing uplift from commercial payers at around 2.5%. On a full-year basis for FY 2024, we now expect operating margins to land at 7.8% to 8.0%, up from our prior guide of 7.5% to 7.8%, reflecting operational discipline amid moderating headwinds.

Looking to FY 2025, our operating margin guidance is 9.0% to 9.6%, implying year-over-year expansion of 100 to 160 basis points. This is underpinned by total revenue growth of 5.0% to 6.0%, with same-facility admissions up 2.5% to 3.5%, outpatient encounters growing 4.0% to 5.0%, and a favorable shift in case mix index of 0.5% to 1.0% as we optimize acuity through advanced surgical service lines, including robotics-assisted procedures like da Vinci systems, now 25% of our high-acuity OR cases.

Key drivers include labor cost moderation and productivity gains: non-clinical labor inflation decelerated to 4.5% in Q3, expected to trend toward 3.5% in FY 2025 via our "CareForward" workforce optimization program, including AI-driven scheduling with Epic's modules and travel nurse utilization below 5% of total RN hours, down from 12% last year. We've realized $45 million in annualized savings from premium pay reductions, targeting a labor expense ratio of 48% to 49% next year versus 50.2% this year.

Supply chain and non-labor efficiencies project supply costs declining 40 basis points to 22.0% of revenue in FY 2025, leveraging GPO commitments with Vizient and HealthTrust, enhanced by RFID-enabled inventory management across our footprint. Post-Change Healthcare cyber disruption, we've accelerated multi-vendor revenue cycle transition, reducing denials by 15% and improving days in AR to 42 from 48, delivering $30 million in incremental cash flow.

Volume and service line momentum from pent-up elective demand, with orthopedic and cardiovascular admissions up 6% year-over-year, fueled by our joint venture ASC network of 120 facilities. Outpatient revenue mix expands to 52% of total, benefiting from site-neutral trends under the No Surprises Act.

Headwinds factored conservatively: Sunbelt margins expected to expand 200 basis points to 12.5%, driven by population in-migration and Medicaid redetermination tailwinds; Northeast and Midwest face 50 basis point compression to 7.0% due to softer volumes and regulations like New York's transparency mandates; California stable at 8.5%, with AB 72 wage mandates offset by value-based contracts covering 25% of lives.

Reimbursement pressures include a 1.5% drag from CMS IPPS FY2025, with 2.9% increase tempered by adjustments; commercial at 3.0% growth, monitoring Medicare Advantage risks at 35% payer mix. Our 340B optimization yields $120 million in FY2024 savings.

To sustain expansion, we're targeting 10% LOS reduction to 4.2 days via predictive analytics from Cerner Millennium integration, bundled payment pilots with UnitedHealthcare and Blue Cross for joint replacements aiming for 15% ortho volume, adding 20 basis points via shared savings. CapEx at 4.0% of revenue focuses on telehealth EDs and AI triage.

Our FY2025 guide reflects balanced tailwinds like aging demographics and execution amid workforce and payer challenges, positioning us as a margin leader with 18% EBITDA CAGR over three years.

Shifting to trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, which are pivotal in shaping our business model and margin profile amid value-based care and site-neutral pressures. In Q3, total system-wide volumes grew 4.2% year-over-year, driven by outpatient strength. Inpatient admissions were 142,500, flat sequentially but down 1.8% year-over-year, marking three quarters of modest contraction per our negative 1% to flat full-year guidance. Patient days totaled 785,000, with average length of stay up slightly to 5.5 days from 5.4, due to stickier acuity in oncology and cardiac interventions.

Outpatient volumes surged 7.1% year-over-year to 2.8 million encounters, including 1.1 million visits to ASCs and HOPDs up 9.2%, and 1.7 million across clinics and imaging up 5.8%. Outpatient revenue now 58% of net patient service revenue, up from 52% in Q3 2023. Adjusted admissions: inpatient down 2.1% to 165,000, outpatient up 8.4% to 420,000, highlighting migration to procedure-driven outpatient services.

Inpatient drivers include payer scrutiny from OPPS site-neutral policies at 40% of HOPD rates, incentivizing outpatient shifts; observation stays up 12% to 18% of volume; labor constraints at 85% staffing vs. 92% outpatient; post-COVID normalization with electives 1% above pre-pandemic, plus seasonal flu/RSV adding 2,500 days.

Outpatient catalysts: robotics like da Vinci Xi in 65 of 120 ASCs drove 15% increase in hysterectomies/prostatectomies, procedure times down 20%, throughput to 25 cases/OR day; Epic MyChart improved no-shows 18%, same-day access 72%; payer bundles with UnitedHealthcare/Anthem added 25,000 cases at $2,800 average reimbursement up 6%.

Regionally: Southeast (42% volumes) outpatient up 9.5%, inpatient flat, Florida MA at 52%, countered by Tampa/Orlando ASCs; Midwest (28%) inpatient down 3.2%, outpatient 6.1%, investing $150M in HOPDs; West Coast (18%) outpatient 7.8%, Medi-Cal redeterminations offset by telehealth converting 15% virtual to in-person.

Strategically, $2.2 billion capex 2023-2025 for 15 ASCs, 40 clinic pods, CarePath platform targets 10-12% outpatient CAGR to 65% mix; margins 28% outpatient vs. 18% inpatient; Enhancing Oncology Model shifts 20% chemo outpatient, 14% volume bump.

Risks: site-neutral expansion, cybersecurity disrupting 2% scheduling; but liquidity $1.8B, 4.5% net revenue per adjusted admission growth de-risks.

Now, on net patient revenue, which came in at $2.48 billion for the quarter—a robust beat up 8.7% year-over-year from $2.28 billion in Q3 2023, and 4.3% quarter-over-quarter from $2.38 billion in Q2 2024. This is our ninth straight quarter of growth, underscoring resilience across our 52-hospital footprint in 12 states.

Volumes led: adjusted admissions up 6.2% to 142,500, inpatient surgical 9.1% surge as electives 15% above pre-pandemic; ED visits 7.8% to 1.85M via freestanding EDs at 22% mix; outpatient up 12.4% on 14% ASC/HOPD procedures. CMI up 2.8% to 1.92 in neuro-spine/CV; LOS steady 4.7 days. QoQ volumes 3.9%, observation up 5.2% under two-midnight rule.

Pricing: revenue per admission up 2.3% to $17,420, outpacing 1.8% CPI; commercial/managed Medicaid 48% up 150 bps; Medicare 32%, IPPS 3.6% update offset 0.5%; MA stabilized at 18% via plan navigation reducing denials 22%.

Deductions: contractual allowances 28.4% down 80 bps via top payer negotiations (UnitedHealthcare/Anthem/Cigna 42% lives, 4.2% uplift); bad debt down 15% to $42M (1.7%); charity 1.2%; 340B up 11%. Clean claims 96.5%, collections 98%.

Regional: Southeast 11.2% growth on 8% admissions/tourism ED; Midwest 4.1%, Medicaid unwind 7% mitigated by outreach/Molina/Centene.

Strategic validation: ACO REACH $28M savings up 35%; 15 ASCs $65M revenue at 25% margins; Epic migration for CMI lift. FY24 7-9% growth on track.

Revenue per admission—or RPA—came in at $15,420, up 4.8% year-over-year and 1.2% sequentially. Trailing four-quarter growth 6.2%, outpacing 3.5% industry per Vizient. Resilient amid CMS FY2024 2.6% IPPS.

Inpatient RPA from $14,780 to $15,420; CMI up 3.7% to 1.94; observation $12,850.

Drivers: payer mix commercial/managed 48% up 4 points, +$450/admission at 145% Medicare; Medicaid 18% offset by Texas/Florida directed payments +8%. Ortho/neuro RPA +7.2%/6.9% via implant consortium 5% hikes; cardio cath +12% volumes +$320; oncology infusion +9% to $2,800 via 340B/Keytruda expansion 15 sites.

Acuity: DRG weight +4.1% on sepsis +22%, electives 98% pre-COVID; CDI with 3M/Nuance $28M capture.

Tech: Epic Revenue Cycle denial 2.1% from 4.3%, clean claims 97%; RPA dashboard/Strata mid-quarter corrections +3% Midwest; Cerner predictive CMI +1-2% FY2025.

Regional: Sunbelt +6.1% to $16,200 on demographics/Phoenix ramp; Southeast +4.5%; Northeast/Midwest +2.8%, ASC carve-outs.

Outlook: 4-6% annual growth FY2026 via $250M capex neuro-ICUs/Medtronic robotics, Enhancing Oncology bundles +8% premium.

Finally, payer revenue mix: Medicare 38.2% (up 170 bps YoY), Medicaid 18.7% (down 50 bps), commercial 37.4% (down 140 bps), self-pay/other 5.7% (up 20 bps). YTD stable at 37.9%/18.4%/38.1%/5.6%.

Medicare up on Boomer aging +5.5% projected; admissions +4.2%, CMI +1.8% to 1.92 joint DRGs; reimbursements -2.1% IPPS FY2025; Southwest 42%, MA 28%; Northeast 35%.

Medicaid flat volumes, per case -1.4%; expansion states 22% Southeast vs. 14% Ohio; value-based +150 bps margins, readmissions -8%.

Commercial $18,400/case double Medicaid; revenue +5.1% on 2.8% volumes; yield 185% Medicare via 60% top contracts 4-6% bumps PSI-90 tied; Arizona 45%.

Self-pay up on inflation; charity +12% $28M; collections 42% from 38%, bad debt 25%; assistance 65% under 400% FPL.

Trends: Medicare-heavy +250 bps past 24 months like peers; pillars: Oracle Revenue Cycle denials -22% to 14%, HCC +15% $45M; contracting 50/50 split 2026, Anthem CABG/TKA bundles +300 bps; Sunbelt de novos, Midwest tuck-ins.

Q4 Medicare 38-39%, commercial stabilize; risks MA -0.5% 2026, redeterminations +100 bps uninsured; $250M ambulatory investment.

Net revenue for Q3 was $4.8 billion, an increase of 6.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and successful revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $4.0 billion, representing 83.3% of net revenue. We continue to focus on managing costs effectively while investing in growth, particularly in supply chain and labor optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $325 million, or $1.42 per share. We are pleased and confident in achieving our goals.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Kline for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Mark. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our CarePathway program has shown promising results, with a 15% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, now handling 25% of visits, and remote patient monitoring programs that have reduced sepsis mortality by 12% in pilot sites.

Following that, Raj will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Kline. We are focused on streamlining operations across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including AI-powered scheduling with LeanTaaS, reducing hours per patient day by 4%, and supply chain integration with GHX and Vizient, yielding $45 million in savings, which have resulted in significant cost savings and improved patient flow in our EDs and ORs.

Next, Lisa will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Raj. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships—like our recent tuck-ins in Georgia and Texas ASCs—and investing in innovative technologies such as da Vinci robotics and AI clinical tools. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key Sunbelt markets and enhance service offerings through value-based care ACOs covering 45% of Medicare lives.

After that, David will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

David Kim:
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures, including multi-vendor revenue cycle post-Change Healthcare, Nuance AI for coding, and enhanced Epic integrations, bolstering our cybersecurity posture and ensuring HIPAA and regulatory compliance amid rising threats.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator instructions.] Our first question comes from Jamie Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jamie Carter:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of the recent cybersecurity threats on your operations and patient data?

David Kim:
Good morning, Jamie. Recent cybersecurity threats, like the Change Healthcare incident, disrupted about 2% of our Q3 outpatient scheduling initially, but our proactive multi-vendor transitions and enhanced protocols limited downtime to under 48 hours across facilities. No patient data breaches occurred; we accelerated investments in AI-driven threat detection and zero-trust architecture, reducing denial impacts by 15% and maintaining AR days at 42. Our fortress liquidity ensures continued resilience.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
What are your plans for expanding your telehealth capabilities and remote patient monitoring programs?

Dr. Sarah Kline:
Thanks, Sarah. We're scaling telehealth to 30% of visits by FY2025, building on 25% this quarter, with Epic MyChart enhancements for seamless virtual-to-in-person handoffs—converting 15% successfully. Remote monitoring expands to all cardiac and ortho post-op patients, integrating with da Vinci outcomes data, targeting another 10% readmission drop and $20 million in shared savings via bundles with UnitedHealthcare.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Can you provide more details on your strategic partnerships and their potential impact on your business?

Lisa Chen:
Absolutely, Mike. Key partnerships include Vizient GPO for 3-5% supply savings, Olive AI for 22% denial reductions, and payer bundles with Blue Cross and Anthem covering ortho/GI, funneling 25,000 cases at higher yields. Our Tenet-affiliated Georgia tuck-in and ASC JVs add immediate accretion at 14x EBITDA, targeting 65% outpatient mix by 2026 with 10-12% CAGR, boosting margins 100+ bps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Wong:
Mark, on your margin guidance, how are you thinking about labor inflation and reimbursement in FY2025?

Mark Thompson:
Emily, labor inflation is decelerating to 3.5%, with CareForward and float pools keeping us at 48-49% of revenue. Reimbursements bake in CMS 1.5% drag but 3% commercial growth and 340B $120M mitigate. Sunbelt tailwinds offset Northeast pressures, positioning 9.0-9.6% firmly.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the HealthNet Hospitals Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
